name: Probe listener topology
purpose: Binds the profile's HTTP probe handlers to the correct listener. When `probeListener.separatePort` is unset, the handlers bind to the user-traffic listener alongside application routes (fused topology). When `probeListener.separatePort: <N>` is set, the handlers bind to a dedicated HTTP listener on port N that serves only the profile's probe path set (separate-port topology). The topology component also produces the exact-match auth-exempt list the project auth middleware installer consumes so the exemption stays scoped to the resolved probe path set on the listener the handlers actually bound to.
responsibilities: Read the resolved profile's `probeListener.separatePort` value; when unset, register the handler-set handlers at their resolved paths on the user-traffic listener (AC-14104-3).

When `probeListener.separatePort: <N>` is set, open a dedicated HTTP listener on port N and register the handler-set handlers at their resolved paths on that listener; do not register the same handlers on the user-traffic listener (AC-14104-1).
On the separate-port listener, refuse any registration beyond the profile's resolved probe path set; every other request on that listener returns not-found (AC-14104-2).

Emit the auth-exempt list for the topology in effect: on fused topology, the resolved probe path set with exact-match rules on the user-traffic listener; on separate-port topology, the resolved probe path set with exact-match rules on the separate probe listener and the invariant that no auth middleware runs on the separate listener (AC-14107-1, AC-14107-2).
Refuse an exempt-list entry that contains a wildcard character or a trailing slash implying a prefix with `PROBE_EXEMPT_MATCHER_INVALID` (AC-14107-3).
internalStructure: One module exporting a `bindListenerTopology({ profile, handlerSet, userTrafficListener, listenerFactory, exemptListInstaller })` function. When `profile.probeListener.separatePort` is set, the function calls `listenerFactory(port)` to obtain a new listener and registers handler-set entries on it; otherwise the function registers on the injected `userTrafficListener`. The function then hands the resulting exempt-path set to `exemptListInstaller`, which the project auth middleware installer consumes. Returns a `{ bound: [{ listener, path, handler }], exemptSet }` record.

interfaces.name: bindListenerTopology
interfaces.description: bindListenerTopology({ profile, handlerSet, userTrafficListener, listenerFactory, exemptListInstaller }) -> { bound, exemptSet }. Called once at boot after TAC-1502 has built the handler set. The `userTrafficListener` is the project's HTTP router or server object; `listenerFactory(port)` is a project-supplied constructor for a fresh listener on the given port; `exemptListInstaller` is the project's auth-middleware exempt-list installer.

interfaces.name: listenerFactory
interfaces.description: Project-supplied `(port: number) -> Listener` factory. Called only when the separate-port topology is in effect. Returns a new HTTP listener bound to the given port with no middleware installed.

interfaces.name: exemptListInstaller
interfaces.description: Project-supplied installer that receives a `{ listener, paths: string[], matcher: 'exact' }` record and registers the exempt set with the auth middleware on the named listener. Refuses on the topology component's side if the paths carry a wildcard or prefix marker.

dependencies.name: profile resolver
dependencies.description: Reads the frozen profile object for its resolved probe path set and separate-port declaration.

dependencies.name: handler set
dependencies.description: Binds the handlers this component built to the resolved listener.

tradeoffs: The topology component holds no opinion on which listener library the project uses; it delegates listener construction to a project-supplied factory and delegates auth-middleware wiring to a project-supplied installer. That keeps the blueprint portable across Node HTTP servers, framework routers (Express, Hono, Fastify), and Worker-style edge platforms; it costs the project two small wiring functions per apply. The alternative (a blueprint-owned listener implementation) would double as a framework choice and takes on the maintenance load without the portability payoff.
